Niddesa 2.2 Rūpakaṇḍa (The Section on Form)
2.2.3. Analysis of Matter (Rūpavibhatti) 2.2.3.1.

Exposition of Single Categories (Ekakaniddesa) All matter is not exclusively with root-cause, not exclusively rootless, not exclusively dissociated from root-cause, not exclusively conditioned, and not exclusively formed.
It is only form; it is only mundane; it is only with taints; it is only subject to fetters; it is only subject to ties; it is only subject to floods;
it is only subject to yokes; it is only subject to hindrances; it is only adhered to; it is only subject to clinging;
it is only defiled; it is only indeterminate; it is only without an object; it is only non-mental; it is only dissociated from consciousness; it is neither resultant nor productive of result.

It is exclusively undefiled yet subject to defilement; it is not exclusively with applied thought and sustained thought, nor exclusively without applied thought but with sustained thought alone, nor exclusively without applied thought and sustained thought; it is not exclusively accompanied by rapture, nor exclusively accompanied by pleasure, nor exclusively accompanied by equanimity;
it is not exclusively to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation, nor exclusively having roots that are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation.
It neither leads to accumulation nor to diminution; it is neither that of the trainee nor that of the one beyond training; it is limited;
it belongs only to the sense-sphere, not to the fine-material sphere, nor to the immaterial sphere; it is included within the mundane, not the supramundane;
it is indeterminate; it does not lead to liberation; it is cognizable by the six consciousnesses when arisen; it is impermanent; and it is overcome by aging.
Thus is the inclusion of form by way of a single category. This is the exposition of the singlefold.
2.2.3.2. The Exposition of the Twofold: The Analysis of Clinging (Upādābhājanīya).
What is that form which is derived?
The eye-base, the ear-base, the nose-base, the tongue-base, the body-base, the visible-form base,
the sound-base, the odor-base, the taste-base, the femininity faculty, the masculinity faculty, and the life faculty.
Bodily intimation, verbal intimation, the space element, lightness of matter, malleability of matter,
wieldiness of matter, integration of matter, continuity of matter, decay of matter, impermanence of matter, and edible food.
What is that matter which is the eye-base?
That eye which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitive, included within the personal organism, invisible, and impinging—
by means of which invisible and impinging eye one has seen, sees, will see, or may see visible and impinging forms:
this is the eye, this is the eye-base, this is the eye-element, and this is the eye-faculty.
This world is it, these doors are it, this ocean is it; this is the white, this is the field, this is the site,
this is the leader, this is the guide, this is the hither shore, and this empty village is it—
this is that form which is the eye-base (*cakkhāyatana*).
What is that form which is the eye-base?
It is that sensitivity derived from the four great elements, included within the personal organism, invisible and impinging,
by means of which invisible and impinging eye, visible form— which is both visible and impinging— is struck.
Whether it has struck, will strike, or is striking [an object], this is the eye, this is the eye-base,
this is the eye-element, this is the eye-faculty; this is the world, this is the door, this is the ocean, this is the white,
this is the field, this is the site, this is the conduit, this is the leading, this is the hither shore, this is the empty village.
This is that form which is the eye-base.
What is that form which is the eye-base?
It is that eye which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitive, included within the personal organism, invisible, and impinging.

That eye which is non-manifesting but impinging, which has impinged, does impinge, will impinge, or might impinge upon a visible form that is manifesting and impinging— this is the eye, this is the eye-base,
this is the eye-element, this is the eye-faculty, this is the world, this is the door, this is the ocean, this is the white [lotus], this is the field.
This is the basis, this is the guide, this is the leading, this is the near shore;
this is an empty village—this is that form which is the eye-base.
What is that form which is the eye-base?
That eye which, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitivity included within the personal organism, invisible and impinging; that eye depending upon which,
with respect to a visible form, visual contact has arisen, arises, will arise,
or may arise …pe… that eye depending upon which, with respect to a visible form, feeling born of visual contact …pe… perception …pe… [has arisen, arises, will arise, or may arise].
Volition …pe… eye-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising …pe… depending on the eye,
eye-contact with visible forms as its object has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising …pe…
And whatever feeling born of eye-contact, perception born of eye-contact, and volition born of eye-contact arise dependent upon the eye with visible forms as their object...
[and so on] ...perception... [and so on] ...volition... [and so on].
Whether visual consciousness has arisen, is arising, will arise, or is arising, this is the eye, this is the eye-base, this is the eye-element,
this is the eye-faculty; this is the world, this is the gateway, this is the ocean, this is the white [lotus],
this is the field, this is the site, this is the guide, this is the leader, this is the near shore, this is the empty village.
This is that form which is the eye-base.
What is that form which is the ear-base?
That which is the ear, derived from the four great elements, a sensitive materiality included within the personal existence, invisible and impinging.
That ear, invisible and impinging, by which one has heard, hears, will hear, or is hearing sound that is invisible and impinging— this is the ear, this is the ear-base,
this is the ear-element, this is the faculty of the ear; this is the world, this is the gateway, this is the ocean,
this is the white field, this is the site, this is the hither shore, this is the empty village.
This is that form which is the ear-base.
What is that form which is the ear-base?
It is that sensitivity derived from the four great elements, included within the personal organism, invisible and impinging.
In that ear which is non-manifest yet possesses resistance, a sound that is non-manifest yet possesses resistance has struck,
does strike, will strike, or might strike; this is the ear, this is the ear-base, this is the ear-element,
this is the faculty of the ear, this is the world, this is the gateway, this is the ocean, this is the white [field], this is the field, this is the site.
"This hither bank is empty; this is that village"—this is the form that is the ear-base (*sotāyatana*).
What is that form which is the ear-base?
That ear which, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitive faculty included within the personal existence,
invisible and impinging— that ear which is invisible and impinging, and which has impinged, impinges, will impinge,
or might impinge upon sound that is invisible and impinging— this is the ear, this is the ear-base, this is the ear-element.
This ear-faculty is the world, this is the door, this is the ocean, this is the white, this is the field, this is the site,
this is the hither shore, and this is the empty village—
this is that form which is the ear-base (*sotāyatana*).
What is that form which is the ear-base?
It is that ear which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitive, included within the personal organism, invisible, and impinging;
depending on which ear, and having sound as its object, ear-contact has arisen, arises, or will arise.
Or [arose] ... or arises ... whatever ear-dependent feeling born of ear-contact, perception ...
intention ...
or ear-consciousness arose, arises, will arise, or may arise ... pe ... [the same for nose, tongue, body, and mind].
Whatever ear, depending upon which, an auditory contact with sound as its object has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising … [and so on] … whatever ear,
depending upon which, a feeling born of auditory contact with sound as its object … perception … [and so on] … [has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising].
Volition …pe… whether ear-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising, that is the ear, that is the ear-base, that is the ear-element, that is the ear-faculty;
this is the world, this is the gateway, this is the ocean, this is the bright field.
This is the basis; this is the near shore; this is an empty village—this is that form which is the sense base of the ear.
What is that form which is the sense base of the nose?
That nose which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitive matter included within the personal existence,
invisible and impinging— by means of which nose, invisible and impinging, one has smelled, smells, will smell,
or may smell an odor that is invisible and impinging— that is the nose, that is the nose-base, that is the nose-element, and that is the nose-faculty.
This world, these gates, this ocean, this white [cloth], this field, this site, this hither bank, and this empty village—
this is that form which is the sense base of the nose.
What is that form which is the sense base of the nose?
That nose which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitive matter included within the personal existence, invisible and impinging;
wherein, in that invisible and impinging nose, an odor—invisible and impinging—is impinged, is being impinged, will be impinged, or might be impinged:
this is the nose, this is the nose-base, this is the nose-element.
This nose-faculty, this world, these doors, this ocean, this white [cloth], this field, this site,
this hither shore, this empty village—
this is that form which is the nose-base (*ghānāyatana*).
What is that form which is the sense base of the nose?
It is that nose which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitive, included within the personal existence, invisible, and impinging;
that nose which is invisible and impinging, and which strikes against an odor that is invisible and impinging.
Or it has struck against [an object], or it will strike against one, or it has struck against one; this is the nose, this is the nose-base,
this is the nose-element, this is the nose-faculty, this is the world, this is the door, this is the ocean, this is the white [field],
this is the field, this is the site, this is the hither shore, this is the empty village.
This is that form which is the nose-base (*ghānāyatana*).
What is that form which is the nose-base?
It is that nose which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitive matter included within the personal organism, invisible and impinging.
That nose depending upon which, and with reference to which odor, there has arisen, arises, will arise, or might arise nose-contact … [and so on] … that nose depending upon which,
and with reference to which odor, there has arisen, arises, will arise, or might arise feeling born of nose-contact … perception … volition … [and so on].
Nose-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising …pe… depending on the nose,
nose-contact with fragrance as its object has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising …pe… depending on the nose,
feeling born of nose-contact with fragrance as its object …pe…
Perception … [and so on] … volition … [and so on] … nose-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising; this is the nose, this is the nose-base.
This nose-element is the nose-faculty; it is the world, it is the door, it is the ocean, it is the white, it is the field, it is the site, it is the hither shore, and it is the empty village.
This is that form which is the nose-base (*ghānāyatana*).
What is that form which is the tongue-base?
It is that sensitive matter derived from the four great elements, included within the personal organism, invisible and impinging, by means of which tongue—
being invisible and impinging— one has tasted, or tastes, taste— which is invisible and impinging.
Or it will taste, or it has tasted; this is the tongue, this is the tongue-base (*jivhāyatana*), this is the tongue-element (*jivhādhātu*), this is the tongue-faculty (*jivhindriya*).

This is the world, this is the door, this is the ocean, this is the white, this is the field, this is the site, this is the hither shore, this is the empty village—this is that form which is the tongue-base.
What is that form which is the sense-base of the tongue?
It is that sensitivity derived from the four great elements, included within the personal existence, invisible and impinging;
by means of which tongue, which is invisible and impinging, taste—which is invisible and impinging—is struck, or is being struck.
Or it will strike back, or it has struck back; this is the tongue, this is the tongue-base, this is the tongue-element, this is the tongue-faculty, this is the world, this is the door,
this is the ocean, this is the white, this is the field, this is the site, this is the hither shore, this is the empty village—
this is that form which is the tongue-base.
What is that form which is the sense-base of the tongue?
It is that sensitivity derived from the four great elements, included within the personal organism, invisible and impinging;
it is the tongue, invisible and impinging, which has impinged, or impinges, upon taste, which is invisible and impinging.
Or it will strike back, or it has struck back; this is the tongue, this is the tongue-base, this is the tongue-element, this is the tongue-faculty, this is the world, this is the door,
this is the ocean, this is the white [field], this is the field, this is the site, this is the hither shore, this is the empty village—
this is that form which is the tongue-base.
What is that form which is the sense base of the tongue?
It is that sensitivity derived from the four great elements, included within the personal existence, invisible and impinging,
depending upon which tongue and having taste as its object, tongue-contact has arisen, arises, or will arise.
Or [has arisen] or arises …pe… whatever tongue-based feeling born of tongue-contact,
whatever perception …pe… whatever volition …pe… whatever tongue-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or may arise …pe….

Whatever tongue-contact with flavor as its object has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising in dependence on the tongue … [and so on] … whatever feeling born of tongue-contact with flavor as its object … perception … [and so on] … that has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising in dependence on the tongue.

[and so on] ...tongue-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or may arise;
this is the tongue, this is the tongue-base, this is the tongue-element, this is the tongue-faculty, this is the world, this is the door, this is the ocean, this is the white, this is the field.
This is the site, this is the near shore; this is an empty village—this is that form which is the sense base of the tongue.
What is that form which is the sense base of the body?
That body which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitive, included within the personal existence, invisible, and impinging—
by means of which invisible and impinging body one has touched, touches, will touch, or touches a tangible object that is invisible and impinging:
this is the body, this is the body-base, this is the body-element, and this is the body-faculty.

That body which is derived from the four great elements, a sensitivity included within the personal existence,
invisible and impinging; and in that body, which is invisible and impinging, there is a tangible object, invisible and impinging,
which has impinged, impinges, will impinge, or might impinge— this is the body, this is the body-base, this is the body-element.
This body-faculty is the world; this is the door; this is the ocean; this is the white; this is the field; this is the site;
this is the hither shore; this empty village is the body-base—this is that form which is the body-sphere.
What is that form which is the body-base?
It is that body which, derived from the four great elements, is a sensitivity included within the personal organism, invisible and impinging;
that body which, being invisible and impinging, strikes against the invisible and impinging tangible object.
Whether it has struck, will strike, or is striking [an object], this is the body, this is the body-base, this is the body-element, this is the body-faculty;
this is the world, this is the gateway, this is the ocean, this is the white [field], this is the field, this is the site,
this is the hither shore, this is the empty village.
This is that form which is the body-base (*kāyāyatana*).
What is that form which is the body-base?
It is that sensitive matter derived from the four great elements, included within the personal existence, invisible and impinging.
Whatever bodily contact has arisen, arises, will arise, or may arise, depending on this body and having a tangible object as its condition;
whatever feeling born of bodily contact ... perception ... volition ... [arises] depending on this body and having a tangible object as its condition.
Body-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising …pe… depending on which body there has arisen,
arises, will arise, or is arising body-contact with tangible objects as its object …pe… depending on which body there has arisen, arises, will arise,
or is arising feeling born of body-contact with tangible objects as its object …pe…
Perception … [and so on] … volition … body-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising; this is the body, this is the body-base.
This body-element is this body-faculty; it is the world, it is the door, it is the ocean, it is the white, it is the field, it is the site,
it is the hither shore, and it is the empty village—
this is that bodily base (kāyāyatana).
What is that form which is the sense-sphere of form (*rūpāyatana*)?
It is that form derived from the four great elements which possesses visible appearance and is impingent;
it is blue, yellow, red, white, black, crimson, green, the color of a parrot, the color of a mango sprout, long, [short, etc.]... [and so forth].
Short, minute, large, round, circular, square, hexagonal, octagonal, sixteen-sided;
low, high, shadow, heat, light, darkness, cloud, mist, smoke, dust;
the appearance of the color of the moon’s disk, the appearance of the color of the sun’s disk, the appearance of the color of the stars, the appearance of the color of a mirror’s disk.
The appearance of gems, conch shells, pearls, beryl, gold, and silver;
or whatever other form there is that is the appearance of the four great elements derived [from them], visible and impinging—
whatever form is visible and impinging that one has seen, sees, or will see with the eye, which is invisible and impinging.
Or has seen it, or will see it, or is seeing it—this is form, this is the form base (*rūpāyatana*), this is the form element (*rūpadhātu*).
This is that form which is the form base.
What is that form which is the form base?
That form which, derived from the four great elements, is a manifestation of color, visible and impinging;
blue, yellow, red, white, black, crimson, green, the color of a golden mango sprout;
long, short, fine, coarse, round, circular, square, hexagonal, octagonal, or sixteen-sided.
Water, land, shade, sunlight, light, darkness, clouds, mist, smoke, dust;
the appearance of the moon’s disk, the appearance of the sun’s disk, the appearance of the stars, the appearance of a mirror’s surface,
the appearance of gems, conch shells, pearls, beryl, gold, and silver— or whatever else there may be.
There is form derived from the four great elements that is visible and impinging, consisting of color and luster;

in regard to such form—which is visible and impinging—the eye, which is invisible and impinging, has struck, does strike, will strike, or might strike it. This is form, this is the base of form, this is the element of form.
This is that form which is the sphere of visible form (*rūpāyatana*).
What is that form which is the sphere of visible form?
It is that form derived from the four great elements (*mahābhūta*) which has color and luster, is visible, and is impinging—blue... [and so forth].
Yellow, red, white, black, madder-red, green, yellowish-green, the color of mango sprouts;
long, short, fine, coarse, round, circular, square, hexagonal, octagonal, sixteen-sided;
low, high, shadow, sunshine, light, darkness, cloud, mist, smoke, dust, and the disk of the moon.
The appearance of color like that of the solar disc, the appearance of color like that of the stars, the appearance of color like that of the surface of a mirror,
the appearance of color like that of gems, shells, pearls, and beryl, the appearance of color like that of gold and silver,
or whatever other appearance of color there is derived from the four great elements— which is visible and impinging— whatever...
Visible form that is visible and impinging, which has impinged, impinges, will impinge, or might impinge upon the eye—which is invisible and impinging—this is form;
this is the sense-sphere of form; this is the element of form.
This is that form which is the sense-sphere of form.
What is that form which is the form base (*rūpāyatana*)?
It is that form derived from the four great elements (*mahābhūta*) which possesses visible appearance and is impinging;
it is blue, yellow, red, white, black, crimson, green, the color of a parrot, the color of a mango sprout, long...
Short, minute, large, round, circular, square, hexagonal, octagonal, sixteen-sided;
low, high, shadow, glare, light, darkness; cloud, mist, smoke, dust;
the appearance of the color of the moon’s disk, the appearance of the color of the sun’s disk, the appearance of the color of the stars, the appearance of the color of a mirror’s disk.
The appearance of gems, conch shells, pearls, beryl, gold, and silver;
or whatever other form there is that is the appearance of the four great elements derived from them, visible and impinging— whatever form,
having depended upon which, and supported by the eye, visual contact has arisen, arises, or will arise.
Or [arose], or arises, or will arise …pe… whatever form, having depended upon which and supported by the eye,
there arose, arises, will arise, or has arisen feeling born of eye-contact … perception … volition … eye-consciousness …pe….
Whatever eye-contact has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising, conditioned by the eye and having visible form as its object;
whatever feeling born of eye-contact … perception born of eye-contact … [arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising, conditioned by the eye and having visible form as its object] … [and so on].
Volition …pe… whether eye-consciousness has arisen, is arising, will arise, or arises: this is material form, this is the base of material form, this is the element of material form—
this is that material form which is the base of material form.
What is that form which is the sense-sphere of sound?
It is sound derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging:

the sound of a drum, the sound of a kettle-drum, the sound of a conch, the sound of a small drum, the sound of singing, the sound of instrumental music, the sound of clapping, the sound of hand-clapping, and the vocal sounds of sentient beings.
The sound of the collision of elements, the sound of wind, the sound of water,
the sound of humans, the sound of non-humans, or whatever other sound there may be— derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging—
which one hears, or hears, or will hear, with the ear that is invisible and impinging; that sound which is invisible and impinging.

Or whatever sound there is, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, distant or near—all that sound is the sound-base (saddāyatana) and the sound-element (saddhadhātu).
This is that form which is the sound-base.
What is that form which is the sound-base?
Whatever sound there is derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging— such as the sound of a drum, the sound of a tabor, the sound of a conch,
the sound of a small drum, the sound of singing, the sound of instrumental music, the sound of clapping, the sound of hand-clapping,

the vocal sounds of beings, the sounds produced by the collision of elements, the sound of wind, the sound of water, the sound of humans, the sound of non-humans, or whatever other [sound there may be].
There is sound derived from the four great elements that is non-manifesting and impinging;
in regard to which sound—which is non-manifesting and impinging—the ear, which is non-manifesting and impinging, has impinged, does impinge, will impinge, or might impinge.
That is sound; that is the sphere of sound; that is the element of sound.
This is that form which is the sound-base (*saddāyatana*).
What is that form which is the sound-base?
It is sound derived from the four great elements (*mahābhūta*), invisible and impinging, such as the sound of a drum, the sound of a kettle-drum, and so forth.
The sound of a conch, the sound of a drum, the sound of singing, the sound of instrumental music, the sound of clapping, the sound of hand-clapping,
the vocal sound of beings, the sound of the collision of elements, the sound of wind, the sound of water, the sound of humans, the sound of non-humans,
or whatever other sound there may be that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging— this sound which is invisible...
That which is impinging upon the ear—which is non-demonstrable but impinging—whether it has impinged, impinges, will impinge, or might impinge:
this is sound, this is the sound-base (*saddāyatana*), this is the sound-element (*saddhadhātu*).
This is that form which is the sound-base.
What is that form which is the sphere of sound?
It is sound derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging, such as the sound of a drum, the sound of a kettle-drum, the sound of a conch, the sound of a small drum,
the sound of singing, the sound of instrumental music, the sound of clapping, the sound of hand-clapping, and the vocal sounds of sentient beings.
The sound of the collision of elements, the sound of wind, the sound of water, the sound of humans, the sound of non-humans,
or whatever other sound there may be— derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging— which,
having that sound as its object and depending on the ear, has arisen, arises, will arise, or might arise as ear-contact …pe…
Depending on that sound and based on the ear, there has arisen,
arises, will arise, or may arise feeling born of ear-contact … perception … volition … ear-consciousness … [and so forth] … [as appropriate].

Whatever ear-contact, having sound as its object and depending on the ear, has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising … [and so on] … whatever feeling born of ear-contact, perception … [and so on] … having sound as its object and depending on the ear, has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising … [and so on] …
Volition …pe… whether ear-consciousness has arisen, is arising, will arise, or might arise, this sound, this sphere of sound, this sound-element—
this is that form which is the sphere of sound.
What is that form which is the sense-sphere of odors?
It is odor derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging, such as root-odor, heartwood-odor,
bark-odor, leaf-odor, flower-odor, fruit-odor, raw-odor, putrid-odor, and pleasant-odor.
Foul odor, or whatever other odor there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging;
that odor which is invisible and impinging, which one has smelled, smells, will smell, or may smell with the nose, which is itself invisible and impinging—
this is odor, this is the base of odor, this is the element of odor.
This is that form which is the odor-base (*gandhāyatana*).
What is that form which is the odor-base?
It is the odor derived from the four great elements (*mahābhūta*) that is invisible and impinging (*sappaṭigha*), such as the odor of roots, the odor of heartwood, and so forth.
The scent of roots, the scent of leaves, the scent of flowers, the scent of fruits, the scent of raw matter, the scent of putrid matter,
pleasant scent, unpleasant scent, or whatever other scent there may be, derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging—
by means of which invisible and impinging scent the nose, which is itself invisible and impinging, [is affected].
Whether it has struck, is striking, will strike, or might strike—this is odor, this is the odor-base, this is the odor-element.
This is that form which is the odor-base.
What is that form which is the odor-base?
Whatever odor there is derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging— whether it be the odor of roots, the odor of heartwood,
the odor of bark, the odor of leaves, the odor of flowers, the odor of fruits, the odor of raw matter,
the odor of excrement, a pleasant odor, or an unpleasant odor— or whatever other odor there is derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging.
That which is resistant, a fragrance that is non-manifest and resistant, which has struck, strikes, will strike, or might strike the nose—which is non-manifest and resistant:
this is fragrance, this is the fragrance base (*gandhāyatana*), this is the fragrance element (*gandhadhātu*).
This is that form which is the fragrance base.
What is that form which is the sense-sphere of odors?
It is odor derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging, such as root-odor, heartwood-odor,
bark-odor, leaf-odor, flower-odor, fruit-odor, raw-odor, putrid-odor, and sweet-odor.

An unpleasant odor, or whatever other odor there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging, which—having that odor as its object and depending on the nose—has arisen, arises, will arise, or may arise as nose-contact;

[and] that which, having that odor as its object and depending on the nose, is born of nose-contact... pe ... [and] that which, having that odor as its object and depending on the nose, is born of nose-contact.
Feeling … perception … volition … nose-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or may arise … [and so forth] …
Whatever nose-contact has arisen, arises, will arise, or may arise, depending on the nose and having fragrance as its object;

whatever feeling born of nose-contact … perception born of nose-contact … [arisen, arises, will arise, or may arise] depending on the nose and having fragrance as its object. …pe… [and so on for the other mental factors]. …pe…
Volition …pe… if nose-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising, this is odor; this is the base of odor;
this is the element of odor—this is that form which is the base of odor.
What is that form which is the sense-base of taste?

It is taste derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging, consisting of the taste of roots, the taste of trunks, the taste of bark, the taste of leaves, the taste of flowers, and the taste of fruits;
it is sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, and salty.
Whether it be bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, or whatever other taste there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging—
a taste that is invisible and impinging which one has tasted, tastes, will taste, or is tasting with the tongue, which is invisible and impinging—
this is taste, this is the sense base of taste, this is the element of taste.
This is that form which is the sense-sphere of taste.
What is that form which is the sense-sphere of taste?
It is the taste derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging, such as the taste of roots, the taste of trunks, [the taste of branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, and so forth].
The taste of roots, the taste of stalks, the taste of leaves, the taste of flowers, the taste of fruits; sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, salty, alkaline, astringent, mild, or harsh;
or whatever other taste there may be derived from the four great elements—non-manifest and impinging—in which non-manifest and impinging taste the tongue is non-manifest.

That which is with resistance, has struck, is striking, will strike, or might strike; that which is taste, this is the sense-sphere of taste, this is the element of taste—this is that form which is the sense-sphere of taste.
What is that form which is the sense-sphere of taste?

Whatever taste there is derived from the four great elements—whether invisible and impinging, or the taste of roots, the taste of trunks, the taste of bark, the taste of leaves, the taste of flowers, or the taste of fruits;
whether sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, salty, alkaline, astringent, or acrid;
whether delicious or undelicious; or whatever other taste there may be derived from the four great elements.
Depending [on these], there is that invisible and impinging taste,
which has struck, strikes, will strike, or might strike against the invisible and impinging tongue; this is taste, this is the sense-sphere of taste, this is the element of taste.
This is that form which is the sense-sphere of taste.
What is that form which is the sense-sphere of taste?
It is the taste derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging, such as the taste of roots, the taste of trunks, and so forth.

The taste of roots, the taste of stalks, the taste of leaves, the taste of flowers, the taste of fruits; sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, salty, alkaline, astringent, mild, harsh, pleasant, or unpleasant;
or whatever other taste there may be, derived from the four great elements, invisible and impinging, which, having that taste as its object and depending on the tongue, gives rise to tongue-contact.

... arises, or has arisen, or will arise, or is arising ... [and so on] ... whatever taste, having depended upon which and with the tongue as its basis, there arises feeling born of tongue-contact ... perception ...
volition ... [and so on].
Tongue-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising …pe… that tongue-contact,
conditioned by the tongue and having taste as its object, has arisen, arises, will arise,
or is arising …pe… that feeling born of tongue-contact, conditioned by the tongue and having taste as its object …pe…
Perception … [and so on] … volition … [and so on] … tongue-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising; this is taste, this is the base of taste, this is the element of taste.
This is that form which is the sense base of taste.
What is that form which is the female faculty?
That which in a woman is the female characteristic, the female mark, the female demeanor, the female appearance, the state of being female, and the female nature.
This is that form which is the femininity faculty.
What is that form which is the masculinity faculty?
That which is the male characteristic, the male sign, the male deportment, the male appearance, the state of being male, and the nature of being male in a man.
This is that material form which is the male faculty.
What is that material form which is the life faculty?
It is the life-span, the persistence, the subsistence, the maintenance, the going-on, the occurrence, the preservation, the vitality, and the life-faculty of those material phenomena.
This is that material form which is the life-faculty.
What is that material form which is bodily intimation?
It is the bodily movement of one who is approaching or departing, whether with a wholesome mind, an unwholesome mind, or an indeterminate mind.
Or, in looking forward, or looking around, or contracting, or extending the body— the stiffening, the rigidity,
the state of being rigid, the intimation, the making known, the state of having made known—
this is that material form which is bodily intimation (*kāyaviññatti*).
What is that material form which is vocal intimation?
Whatever speech, utterance, discourse, enunciation, sound, vocal action, speech, or vocal expression there is of a wholesome mind, an unwholesome mind, or an indeterminate mind—
this is called speech.
That which is the intimation, the making known, the state of having been made known by that speech—
this is that material form called vocal intimation.
What is that material form called the space element?
That space which has become space, the void which has become a void, the cavity which has become a cavity, not obstructed by the four great elements—
this is that form which is the space element (*ākāsadhātu*).
What is that form which is the lightness of form (*rūpassa lahutā*)?
That which is the lightness of form, its state of being light, its lack of heaviness, its lack of rigidity—
this is that form which is the lightness of form.
What is that form which is the malleability of form?
That which is the plasticity, softness, non-hardness, and non-rigidity of form—
this is that form which is the plasticity of form.
What is that form which is the wieldiness of form?
That which is the wieldiness of form, its state of wieldiness, its condition of wieldiness—
this is that form which is the wieldiness of form.
What is that form which is the integration of form?
Whatever is the accumulation of the sense bases, that is the growth of form—
this is that form which is the growth of form.
What is that form which is the continuity of form?
That which is the accumulation of form is the continuity of form—
this is that form which is the continuity of form.
What is that form which is the aging of form?
That which is the aging of form, its decrepitude, brokenness, graying of hair, wrinkling of skin, the decline of the life-span, and the maturation of the faculties—
this is that form which is the aging of form.
What is that form which is the impermanence of form?
That which is the exhaustion, passing away, breaking up, dissolution, impermanence,
and disappearance of form— this is that impermanence of form.
What is that form which is physical food?
Rice, millet, barley meal, fish, meat, milk, curd, ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, molasses,
or whatever other material form exists in various regions that is eaten by the mouths, chewed with the teeth, swallowed down the throat,
and fills the belly of those various beings, and by means of which nutritive essence beings subsist— this is called edible food.
This is that form which is edible food.
This is that form which is derived;
it is what is to be maintained by the derived.
The first recitation section in the Chapter on Matter.
What is that matter which is not derived?
The sphere of the tangible and the water element.
What is that form which is the sense base of the tangible?
It is the earth element, the fire element, and the air element;
hardness, softness, smoothness, roughness, pleasant contact, painful contact, heaviness, and lightness—whatever tangible object is invisible and impinging, [to be experienced] by the body.
That which has been touched, is being touched, will be touched, or is being touched by that which is non-indicative and impinging—
this is tangibility, this is the tangibility base, this is the tangibility element:
this is that form which is the tangibility base.
What is that form which is the sphere of the tangible?

It is the earth element, the fire element, and the air element; hardness, softness, smoothness, roughness, pleasant contact, painful contact, heaviness, and lightness—whatever is tangible, invisible, and impinging.
The body is non-manifesting and impinging; it has impinged, it impinges, it will impinge, or it might impinge.
This is tangibility, this is the sense base of tangibility, this is the element of tangibility—this is that form which is the sense base of tangibility.
What is that form which is the sense base of the tangible?
It is the earth element, the fire element, and the air element; hardness, softness, smoothness, roughness, pleasant contact, painful contact, heaviness, and lightness;
whatever is tangible, invisible, and impinging upon the body, which is itself invisible.
That which has resistance and has struck, strikes, will strike, or might strike, is tangibility;
it is the sense-sphere of tangibility, it is the element of tangibility—
this is that form which is the sense-sphere of tangibility.
What is that form which is the sense base of the tangible?
It is the earth element, the fire element, and the air element;
hardness, softness, smoothness, roughness, pleasant contact, painful contact, heaviness, and lightness—whatever tangible object, having been the basis for tactile contact dependent on the body.
...has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising ... [and so on] ... whatever tangible object one takes as a basis, depending on the body, there arises feeling born of body-contact ... perception ...
volition ... [and so on].
Body-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising …pe… whatever body-contact,

having tangible objects as its object and depending on the body, has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising …pe… whatever feeling born of body-contact, having tangible objects as its object and depending on the body, [has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising] …pe…
Perception …pe… volition …pe… body-consciousness has arisen, arises, will arise, or is arising: this is tangibility, this is the sense-sphere of tangibility, this is the element of tangibility.
This is that form which is the sphere of the tangible.
What is that form which is the water element?
That which is water, watery, viscous, viscosity, and the cohesion of form.
This is that form which is the water element.
This is that form which is not derived.
What is that form which is clung-to?
The eye-base, ear-base, nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, femininity-faculty, masculinity-faculty, life-faculty;
or whatever other material form there is produced by karma having been performed, namely:
the visible-form base, odor base, taste base, tangible-object base, the space element, the water element, the integration of matter, the continuity of matter, and physical nutriment.
This is that form which is clung-to.
What is that form which is not clung-to?
The sphere of sound, bodily intimation, verbal intimation, lightness of form, malleability of form, and wieldiness of form.
The aging of form, the impermanence of form; or whatever other form there is that is not due to karma having been performed, namely:

the sphere of visible forms, the sphere of odors, the sphere of tastes, the sphere of tangibles, the element of space, the element of cohesion, the integration of form, the continuity of form, and physical nutriment.
This is that form which is not clung-to (anupādinna).
What is that form which is both clung-to and subject to clinging (upādinnupādāniya)?
The eye-base …pe… the body-base, the femininity-faculty, the masculinity-faculty, the life-faculty, or whatever other [form] there may be.
There is matter that, because it has been performed as kamma, consists of the visible-form base, the odor base, the flavor base, the tangible base, the space element,
the water element, the integration of matter, the continuity of matter, and physical nutriment—
this is that matter which is both acquired by clinging and favorable to clinging.
What is that form which is not clung-to but is subject to clinging?
It is the sphere of sound, bodily intimation, verbal intimation, lightness of form, malleability of form, wieldiness of form, decay of form, and impermanence of form;
or whatever other form exists that is not born of karma already performed.
The visible-form base, the odor base, the flavor base, the tangible-base, the space element, the water element, the integration of form,
the continuity of form, and physical nutriment—
this is that form which is not clung-to but is subject to clinging.
What is that form which is visible?
The sphere of visible form (rūpāyatana)—
this is that form which is visible.
What is that form which is non-demonstrable?
The eye-base …pe… edible food—
this is that form which is non-demonstrable.
What is that form which is with resistance?
The eye-base, the ear-base, the nose-base, the tongue-base, the body-base, the visible-form base, the sound-base, the odor-base, the taste-base, and the tangible-object base—
this is that form which is with resistance.
What is that form which is non-reactive (appaṭigha)?
The female faculty … [and so on] … edible food—
this is that form which is non-reactive.
What is that form which is a faculty?
The eye-faculty, the ear-faculty, the nose-faculty, the tongue-faculty, the body-faculty, the female-faculty, the male-faculty, and the life-faculty—
this is that form which is a faculty.
What is that form which is not a faculty?
The sense-sphere of visible forms …pe… edible food—
this is that form which is not a faculty.
What is that form which is a great primary element?
The tangible base, the water element—
this is that form which is a great primary element.
What is that form which is not a great primary element?
The eye-base …pe… edible food—
this is that form which is not a great primary element.
What is that form which is intimation?
Bodily intimation and verbal intimation—
this is that form which is intimation.
What is that form which is not intimation?
The eye-base … down to … edible food—
this is that form which is not intimation.
What is that form which is mind-originated?

It is bodily intimation and verbal intimation; or whatever other form there is that is born of mind, caused by mind, and originated by mind—namely, the sphere of visible forms, the sphere of sounds, the sphere of odors, the sphere of tastes, the sphere of tangibles, the space element, and the water element.
The lightness of form, the malleability of form, the wieldiness of form, the integration of form, the continuity of form, and physical nutriment—
this is that form which is mind-originated.
What is that form which is not mind-originated?
The eye-base …pe… the body-base, the femininity faculty, the masculinity faculty, the life faculty, the aging of matter, the impermanence of matter;
or whatever other matter there is that is not born of mind, not caused by mind, and not produced by mind—
the visible-form base, the sound base, the odor base, the flavor base, the tangible-base, the space element, and the water element.
The lightness of matter, the malleability of matter, the wieldiness of matter, the integration of matter, the continuity of matter, and physical nutriment—
this is that matter which is not mind-originated.
What is that matter which is co-existent with mind?
Bodily intimation and verbal intimation—
this is that material form which is co-nascent with consciousness.
What is that material form which is not co-nascent with consciousness?
The eye-base …pe… edible food—
this is that material form which does not arise simultaneously with consciousness.
What is that material form which follows upon consciousness?
Bodily intimation and verbal intimation—
this is that material form which follows the mind.
What is that material form which does not follow the mind?
The eye-base …pe… edible food—
this is that material form which does not follow the mind.
What is that material form which is internal?
The eye-base …pe… the body-base—
this is that form which is internal.
What is that form which is external?
The visible-form base …pe… edible food—
this is that external matter.
What is that matter which is gross?
The eye-base …pe… the tangible-object-base—
this is that gross material form.
What is that subtle material form?
The faculty of femininity … [and so on] … edible food—
this is that subtle matter.
What is that matter which is distant?
The faculty of femininity … [and so on] … edible food—
this is that material form which is distant.
What is that material form which is near?
The eye-base …pe… the tangible-object-base—
this is that form which is proximate.
What is that form which is the basis for eye-contact?
The eye-base—
this is that material form which is the basis for eye-contact.
What is that material form which is not the basis for eye-contact?
The ear-base …pe… edible food—
this is that material form which is not the basis for eye-contact.
What is that material form which [is not the basis] for feeling born of eye-contact …pe…?
Is it the basis for perception … pe … for volition … pe … for eye-consciousness?
The eye-base—
this is that form which is the basis for eye-consciousness.
What is that form which is not the basis for eye-consciousness?
The ear-base …pe… edible food—
this is that material form which is not the basis for eye-consciousness.
What is that material form [which is the basis] for ear-contact …pe…?
What is the basis for nose-contact …pe… tongue-contact …pe… body-contact?
The body-base—
this is that form which is the basis for body-contact.
What is that form which is not the basis for body-contact?
The eye-base …pe… edible food—this is that material form which is not the basis for body-contact.
What is that material form [which is not the basis] for feeling born of body-contact? …pe…
Is it the basis for perception … pe … for volition … pe … for body-consciousness?
The body-base—
this is that form which is the basis for body-consciousness.
What is that form which is not the basis for body-consciousness?
The eye-base …pe… edible food—
this is that material form which is not the basis for body-consciousness.
This is the "Duality of Bases" (Vatthuduka).
What is that form which is the object of eye-contact?
The sense-sphere of visible forms—
this is that form which is the object of eye-contact.
What is that form which is not the object of eye-contact?
The eye-base …pe… edible food—
this is that form which is not the object of eye-contact.
What is that form which [is the object] for feeling born of eye-contact … perception … volition …?
What is the object of eye-consciousness?
The sphere of visible forms—
this is that form which is the object of eye-consciousness.
What is that form which is not the object of eye-consciousness?
The eye-base …pe… edible food—
this is that form which is not the object of eye-consciousness.
What is that form which is the basis for ear-contact … pe … nose-contact … pe … tongue-contact … pe …?
What is the object of body-contact?
The sphere of the tangible—
this is that form which is the object of body-contact.
What is that form which is not the object of body-contact?
The eye-base … [and so on] … edible food—
this is that form which is not the object of body-contact.
What is that form which, for the feeling born of body-contact …pe… for perception …pe… for volition …pe…?
What is the object of body-consciousness?
The sphere of the tangible—
this is that form which is the object of body-consciousness.
What is that form which is not the object of body-consciousness?
The eye-base …pe… edible food—
this is that form which is not the object of body-consciousness.
The Pair on Objects.
What is that form which is the eye-base?
That eye which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitive matter ... [as before] ... this is an empty village.
This is that form which is the eye-base.
What is that form which is not the eye-base?
The ear-base … [and so on] … edible food.
This is that form which is not the eye-base.
What is that form which is the ear-base?
…pe… the nose-base? …pe…
The tongue-base …pe… the body-base? That body which,
derived from the four great elements, is sensitive …pe… this is an empty village.
This is that form which is the body-base (*kāyāyatana*).
What is that form which is not the body-base?
The eye-base …pe… edible food.
This is that form which is not the body-base (*kāyāyatana*).
What is that form which is the visible-form base (*rūpāyatana*)?
That form which, derived from the four great elements, is the appearance of color... [and so on] ...this is the element of visible form (*rūpadhātu*).
This is that form which is the base of form.
What is that form which is not the base of form?
The eye-base …pe… edible food.
This is that form which is not the sphere of visible forms (*rūpāyatana*).
What is that form which is the sphere of sounds (*saddāyatana*)? ... [and so on] ...
the sphere of odors (*gandhāyatana*)? ... [and so on] ...
The taste-base …pe… the tangible-base?
It is the earth element …pe… this is the tangible element.
This is that form which is the sphere of the tangible.
What is that form which is not the sphere of the tangible?
The eye-sphere … [and so on] … edible food.
This form is not the tangible base.
This concludes the dyad of bases.
What is that form which is the eye element?
The eye-base—
this is that form which is the eye-element.
What is that form which is not the eye-element?
The ear-base …pe… edible food—
this is that form which is not the eye-element.
What is that form which is the ear-element …pe…?
The nose element …pe… the tongue element …pe… the body element?
The body-base—
this is that form which is the body-element.
What is that form which is not the body-element?
The eye-base …pe… edible food—

The sphere of visible forms …pe… edible food.
This is that external form which is not the aging of form.
What is that internal form which is not the impermanence of form?
The eye-base …pe… the body-base.
This is that internal form which is not the impermanence of form.
What is that external form which is the impermanence of form?

What is that external form which is not the impermanence of external form?
The sense-sphere of visible forms …pe… edible food.
This is that external form which is not impermanent.
What is that internal form which is not edible food?
The eye-base …pe… the body-base.

Rice, millet, barley, fish, meat, milk, curd, ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, and molasses.

Thus is the compendium of material form by way of threefold classification.

2.2.3.6. The Hexad:
The visible-form base is form cognizable by the eye; the sound base is form cognizable by the ear;
the odor base is form cognizable by the nose; the flavor base is form cognizable by the tongue; the tangible-base is form cognizable by the body.
Visible form; all visible form; visible form cognizable by the mind.
Thus is the compendium of visible form by way of sixfold division.
This concludes the hexad.
2.2.3.7. The Group of Seven:
The visible-form base is form cognizable by the eye; the sound base is form cognizable by the ear;
the odor base is form cognizable by the nose; the flavor base is form cognizable by the tongue; the tangible base is form cognizable by the body.
Visible form, the visible-form base, the sound base, the odor base, the flavor base, the tangible-object base,
and the form cognizable by the mind-element— all such form is form cognizable by the mind-consciousness-element.
Thus is the compendium of form by way of sevenfold division.
The Group of Seven.
2.2.3.8. The Group of Eight.
The visible-form base is form cognizable by the eye; the sound base is form cognizable by the ear; the odor base...
Form cognizable by the nose; form as the taste-base cognizable by the tongue; agreeable tangible object, pleasant contact, form cognizable by the body;
disagreeable tangible object, painful contact, form cognizable by the body;
the base of visible forms, the base of sounds, the base of odors, the base of tastes, the base of tangible objects, and form cognizable by the mind-element.
All form is form cognizable by the mind-consciousness element.
Thus is the compendium of form by way of eightfold division. This concludes the section on the octad.
2.2.3.9. The Group of Nine.
What is that form which is the eye-faculty?
That eye which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitive matter … [as before] … this is an empty village.
This is that material form which is the eye-faculty.
What is that material form which is the ear-faculty …pe… the nose-faculty …pe…?
The tongue faculty …pe… the body faculty …pe… the female faculty …pe…
The male faculty …pe… the life faculty?
That which is the life-span, the persistence, the maintenance, the upkeep, the carrying on, the subsistence, the preservation, the vitality, and the life-faculty of those material phenomena.
This is that material form which is the life-faculty (*jīvitindriya*).
What is that material form which is not a faculty?
The sphere of visible forms (*rūpāyatana*) …pe… edible food (*kabaḷīkāra-āhāra*).
This is that form which is not a faculty.
Thus is the compendium of form by way of ninefold classification.
The Ninefold.
2.2.3.10. The Decad.
What is that form which is the eye-faculty?
That eye which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitivity … [as before] … this is an empty village.
This is that material form which is the eye-faculty.
What is that material form which is the ear-faculty …pe… the nose-faculty …pe…?
The tongue faculty …pe… the body faculty …pe… the female faculty …pe…
The male faculty …pe… the life faculty?
That which is the life-span, the persistence, the maintenance, the upkeep, the subsistence, the endurance, the preservation, the vitality, and the life-faculty of those material phenomena.
This is that material form which is the life-faculty.
What is that material form which is not a faculty but is impinging?
The base of visible forms …pe… the base of tangible objects.
This is that material form which is not a faculty and is impinging.
What is that material form which is not a faculty and is non-impinging?
Bodily intimation … [and so on] … edible food.
This is that form which is not a faculty and is non-reactive.
Thus is the compendium of form by way of tenfold classification.
The Decad.
2.2.3.11. The Set of Eleven.
What is that form which is the eye-base?
That eye which, derived from the four great elements, is sensitivity … [as before] … this is an empty village.
This is that form which is the eye-base.
What is that form which is the ear-base? ...pe...
the nose-base? ...pe...
The tongue-base …pe… the body-base …pe… the visible-form base …pe…
The sense-sphere of sound …pe… the sense-sphere of odor …pe… the sense-sphere of taste …pe…
What is the tangible base?
The earth element …pe… this is the tangible element;
this is that material form which is the tangible base.
What is that form which is non-manifesting, non-reactive, and included within the sphere of mental phenomena (dhammāyatana)?
The female faculty … [and so on] … edible food—
this is that form which is non-manifesting, non-reactive, and included within the sphere of mental phenomena.
Thus is the compendium of material form by way of elevenfold classification.
The group of eleven.
The eighth recitation section.
The Analysis of Matter.
